thread:
emma: hey team :wave: I'm a new hire (emma) — trying to run the quickstart. Do I use a hosted API key or the sandbox key? Where do I find them and what's the default rate limit for sandbox? Also how do I request a higher quota if I need it this week? Thanks!

matt: Welcome emma! For experiments use the sandbox key (Console -> Settings > API keys -> Sandbox). Hosted keys are for prod and tied to billing. Sandbox defaults are small: ~60 req/min and ~3 req/sec for most new accounts, and there are soft token/day caps for onboarding. If you need more for a short test, we can bump you.

emma: thanks — where is the sandbox key in the UI? I only see an "API keys" section but no sandbox label.

devops-bot: Automated notice: New users should get a sandbox key provisioned within 10 minutes of account creation. If you don't see one, file a ticket or run the internal check: `curl -s https://internal-api.redwood.ai/users/me/keys` (SSO required).

matt: In the Console it's under Settings > API Keys > Sandbox Keys. If missing, DM @sarah or open a ticket in #help with subject 'missing sandbox key' and include your email.

sarah: @emma DM'd you the key and a quickstart snippet. Example usage (replace $SANDBOX_KEY):
```
curl -X POST https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBOX_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rl-1","input":"hello"}'
```

emma: got it, thanks! If I hit the rate limit during demos, what's the best temporary workaround?

matt: For bursts: client-side exponential backoff + jitter and retry on 429. If you need steady higher throughput during onboarding, submit a sandbox quota request at https://intranet.redwood.ai/quota-request (pick 'sandbox onboarding' and explain the test). DevEx usually replies same day for onboarding requests.

emma: perfect. one last q — do sandbox requests show up on billing? I don't want to accidentally charge the team.

sarah: Sandbox usage is covered by onboarding credits and doesn't bill your corporate account. We still track heavy usage and may cap to keep shared resources fair; if you need production-level load, request a hosted key or Dedicated capacity.

mike: fwiw if you're testing streaming endpoints, append `?stream=true` and try to keep concurrent connections low to avoid socket limits — streaming counts against rate/connection limits differently.

ema: thanks all :rocket:
